answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove the work was duplicated or invalid. A Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so multiplying accounts multiplies capital at risk; identities cannot be created for free just by changing names. Audits still need to catch fraud, and a zephyr of dune dust can settle on ferrous rails without affecting the mechanism.
